## ToolExecutionApi  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * Operations available to one tool invocation. A plain object, so a wrapper can spread it. Every operation rejects after
 * the invocation ends.
 */
export interface ToolExecutionApi<TDetails extends JsonValue = JsonValue, C extends JsonValue = JsonValue>
	extends DocumentObserver,
		DocumentReader {
	readonly taskId: TaskId;
	readonly conversationId: ConversationId;
	readonly callId: string;
	/** Why this run started after a park; undefined on a fresh call, and in `cancel`. */
	readonly wake: WakeReason | undefined;
	/** What the call last parked with; undefined on a fresh call or after a park without one. */
	readonly checkpoint: C | undefined;
	/** The tool task's phase snapshot. */
	readonly registry: RegistrySnapshot;
	/** The calling conversation's agent, as the tool task's phase resolved it. */
	agent(context: Context): Promise<Agent>;
	/** The current `HarnessOptions.models`, read at each access: the catalog, credentials, and request transforms. */
	readonly models: Models;
	/** Built by `HarnessOptions.env` for this call; `undefined` without an environment. */
	readonly env: ExecutionEnv | undefined;
	/** The Harness clock (`HarnessOptions.now`), for times a rerun after a restart compares against. */
	now(): number;
	/**
	 * Append running output; it becomes the result's `output` when the result omits it. `skipped` counts output
	 * omitted before the chunk, as reported by an environment given `outputWindow` (`ShellOutputInfo.skipped`).
	 */
	output(chunk: string | Uint8Array, skipped?: ShellOutputSkip): void;
	/**
	 * The tail this call's output keeps and the pace of its progress commits, for `ShellExecOptions.window`; `undefined`
	 * when the tool keeps the head of its output, which cannot accept skips. A wrapper that replaces `output` and
	 * transforms text must also replace this with `undefined`, so skipped text cannot bypass its transform.
	 */
	readonly outputWindow: ShellOutputWindow | undefined;
	/**
	 * The output retained so far, as the model will see it when the result omits `output`, and whether earlier output was
	 * dropped; for a tool that also returns that text in its `structuredOutput`.
	 */
	retainedOutput(): { readonly text: string; readonly truncated: boolean };
	/** Record a model-visible remark about this call. */
	diagnostic(diagnostic: ToolDiagnostic): void;
	/** Replace running details; the last value becomes the result details when the result omits `details`. */
	details(value: TDetails, context: Context): Promise<void>;
	/** A commit of this call's task; `options` may defer storing it (`CommitPersistence`). */
	commit<T>(change: (tx: Tx) => T | Promise<T>, context: Context, options?: CommitOptions): Promise<T>;
	memo<T extends JsonValue>(name: string, context: Context): Promise<T | undefined>;
	memo<T extends JsonValue>(name: string, candidate: T, context: Context): Promise<T>;
	/** A signal key's committed state in this call's task, as `TaskRuntime.readSignal()`. */
	readSignal<T>(token: SignalToken<T>, key: string, context: Context): Promise<SignalState<T> | undefined>;
	/**
	 * Create a task in one commit. A child task of a tool that is not replay-safe defaults to `abandonOnRestart`: the
	 * tool never resumes after a restart, so nothing awaits the child then. With a `key`, validated like a nested call's,
	 * the task is recorded under it in the same commit, and a later call with the key, in this run, a rerun, or a run
	 * after a wake, returns that task; another task kind, other input, or a key a nested call uses throws. After a wake
	 * (`wake` set) a key is required.
	 */
	createTask<I, S extends { phase: string }, R, H extends object>(
		task: Task<I, S, R, H>,
		input: I,
		options: Omit<TaskOptions, "conversationId"> & { readonly key?: string },
		context: Context,
	): Promise<TaskId<R>>;
	getTask<R>(id: TaskId<R>, context: Context): Promise<TaskRecord<JsonValue, JsonValue, R> | undefined>;
	waitForTask<R>(id: TaskId<R>, context: Context): Promise<SettledTask<R>>;
	/** Invocation-bound handle of an existing conversation, such as one this tool created in `commit()`. */
	conversation(id: ConversationId, context: Context): Promise<ConversationHandle | undefined>;
	/**
	 * Run tool `name` as a nested call of this one and wait for its result. The nested call is its own `pi.tool` task,
	 * owned by this call: it resolves the tool among the conversation's tools, validates, runs the `ToolTask` hooks (which
	 * see `call.parent`), applies output limits and the tool's replay policy, and reports progress in `pi.live.nestedTools`.
	 * Its result returns here instead of entering the transcript. A call that is blocked, invalid, throws, is interrupted,
	 * or is aborted returns an `isError` result.
	 *
	 * The nested call's key names it within this call; its call ID is `<callId>/<key>`. By default the key is the call's
	 * position among this invocation's nested calls, `1`, `2`, ... An explicit `key` must be non-empty, without `/`, not
	 * `__proto__`, and not a positive integer, so it never collides with a default one. After a wake (`wake` set) the
	 * same position may mean another call, so a key is required. A rerun of a replay-safe tool
	 * that makes a call with a used key, by calling in the same order or by passing the same `key`, gets that nested call
	 * back, finished or still running, instead of starting another. A nested call a crash interrupted before its result
	 * committed follows its own replay policy, so this is not exactly-once execution. Reusing a key with another tool or
	 * other arguments throws. A tool that is not replay-safe never reruns: after a restart, its unfinished nested calls
	 * are abandoned (`TaskOptions.abandonOnRestart`) before they run again.
	 *
	 * `progress: false` commits no running output, details, or diagnostics to the nested call's slot, only its status;
	 * the result still carries its details and diagnostics, and a schema-less tool's output as `structuredOutput`. An
	 * interrupted or aborted call's result is built from its slot, so it then has none of them. Either way, programs never
	 * get the partial output of an interrupted or aborted call.
	 *
	 * Nested calls run as soon as they are made, whatever their `executionMode`; the caller decides what runs at once by
	 * what it awaits. Cancelling `context` stops only the wait; the nested call runs on. When this call settles, nested
	 * calls it left running are aborted first. A nested result's `usage` is already counted under its tool; a result
	 * that passes it on counts it again. Rejects, instead of returning a result, once `execute()` has returned, when this
	 * call is aborted, or when the Harness closes.
	 *
	 * Awaiting a nested call holds this call's invocation for as long as it takes, also while it is parked; a tool that
	 * starts calls with `wait: false` and parks on their tasks (`{ kind: "wait", on }`) lets the Session go idle instead.
	 */
	executeTool(
		name: string,
		args: JsonObject,
		context: Context,
		options?: { readonly key?: string; readonly progress?: boolean; readonly wait?: true },
	): Promise<NestedToolExecutionResult>;
	/** As above, but returns once the nested call is started or found, with a handle to its result. */
	executeTool(
		name: string,
		args: JsonObject,
		context: Context,
		options: { readonly key?: string; readonly progress?: boolean; readonly wait: false },
	): Promise<NestedToolCall>;
}

## ToolExecutionMode  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Whether the tools of one round run at once or one after another in call order. */
export type ToolExecutionMode = "parallel" | "sequential";

## ToolExecutionResult  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect, durable-effect, guard-effect; durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * What a tool returns, on three channels: `output` for the model, `structuredOutput` for programs that call the tool
 * (`executeTool()` callers, code mode scripts), and `details` for UIs.
 */
export type ToolExecutionResult<TDetails extends JsonValue = JsonValue> = {
	/** For the model. Omitted: the retained `output()` text. */
	readonly output?: ToolResultMessage["content"];
	/**
	 * For programs. Required unless `isError` when the tool declares `structuredOutputSchema`, and validated against it;
	 * not allowed without one, where programs get the output itself (`NestedToolExecutionResult.structuredOutput`).
	 */
	readonly structuredOutput?: JsonValue;
	readonly isError?: boolean;
	/** Omitted: the last `details()` value becomes the details. */
	readonly details?: TDetails;
	/** Added after those recorded through `api.diagnostic()`. */
	readonly diagnostics?: readonly ToolDiagnostic[];
	/** Spend of the execution itself, such as a model call; stored on the result and in `pi.usage.tools`. */
	readonly usage?: Usage;
	readonly control?: ToolControl;
	/** A result is no park (`ToolPark`): only parks have a `kind`. */
	readonly kind?: never;
};

## ToolHookCall  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect via ToolHooks
/** A call as tool hooks see it; `parent` is set for a nested call, one a running tool made through `executeTool()`. */
export type ToolHookCall = ToolCall & {
	readonly parent?: { readonly taskId: TaskId; readonly callId: string };
};

## ToolHooks  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Hooks of the built-in tool task, for model-issued and nested calls. */
export interface ToolHooks {
	/**
	 * Before intent; `arguments` replace the call's arguments, and the first `block` or `sleep` stops the chain. A throw
	 * blocks. A `sleep` parks the call before it runs (spec suspendable §5): every wake, and every registry change, runs
	 * the whole `call` phase again, so a gate reads the key it waited on with `api.readSignal()` and passes, blocks, or
	 * sleeps on a new key. A sleep that breaks a rule ends the call `invalid_park`.
	 */
	beforeTool(
		call: ToolHookCall,
		api: HookApi,
		context: Context,
	): HookResult<{
		readonly arguments?: JsonObject;
		readonly block?: string;
		readonly sleep?: GateSleep;
	}>;
	/**
	 * Before the result is committed; replaces the result. Runs on every result the tool task writes: an executed
	 * call's, and the error results the Harness writes itself, told apart by their diagnostic code: a tool that does not
	 * resolve (`tool_unavailable`), invalid arguments (`invalid_arguments`, with `call.arguments` as the model sent
	 * them), a block (`blocked`), and, rebuilt from the call's partial output, an interruption (`interrupted`), the
	 * restart limit (`restart_limit`), and an abort (`aborted`, `abandoned`). Once the task was cut off more than
	 * `settings.restartLimit` times the hooks no longer run, since they may be what cuts it off, nor in the last attempt
	 * the scheduler gives an abort handler (restarts at the limit minus one). A result's `structuredOutput` is dropped
	 * when the Harness wrote it (a nested call a hook turns into a success gets the bounded output as a schema-less tool's
	 * does), and its `control` applies only to a call that completes (not to an interrupted, cut-off, or aborted one).
	 * An abort's hooks run inside the abort handler, which cannot be aborted: a slow hook delays `Conversation.abort()`.
	 */
	afterTool(
		call: ToolHookCall,
		result: ToolExecutionResult,
		api: HookApi,
		context: Context,
	): HookResult<ToolExecutionResult>;
}

## ToolNamespace  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via defineExtension, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Named bundle of code; installed in a registry and selected by conversations by name. */
/**
 * A named group of tools for code mode: the extension that brings the tools declares it. `description` is one line,
 * shown in the `codemode` prompt section; `instructions` is the longer how-to, returned only by `describeNamespace()`;
 * `searchTools()` searches both.
 */
export type ToolNamespace = { readonly name: string; readonly description: string; readonly instructions?: string };

## ToolPark  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * What `execute()` returns instead of a result to park the call (spec suspendable §4): kind `sleep` until `until`, for
 * `signals`, or both; or kind `wait` for tasks the call's task owns (`on`). The call holds no invocation meanwhile,
 * then runs `execute()` again with the same arguments, `api.wake` saying why, and `api.checkpoint` set to `checkpoint`.
 */
export type ToolPark<C extends JsonValue = JsonValue> = NoResultFields &
	(
		| {
				readonly kind: "sleep";
				readonly checkpoint?: C;
				readonly until?: number;
				readonly signals?: readonly SignalKey<unknown>[];
		  }
		| {
				readonly kind: "wait";
				readonly checkpoint?: C;
				readonly on: readonly TaskId[];
				readonly policy: JoinPolicy;
		  }
	);

## ToolRegistration  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect, guard-effect, subagent-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * Executable tool registered in a registry. Only pi-ai `Tool` fields enter the transcript. `args` are typed by
 * `parameters` (any JSON Schema object; see {@link ToolArgs}), which the Harness validates them against before
 * `execute()`; `defineTool()` infers both generics.
 */
export type ToolRegistration<
	TParameters extends object = object,
	TDetails extends JsonValue = JsonValue,
	C extends JsonValue = JsonValue,
> = Tool<TParameters> & {
	/** Whether an interrupted execution may rerun on recovery. Default `unsafe`. */
	readonly replay?: "safe" | "unsafe";
	/** Default: the settings' `toolExecution`. One sequential call makes its whole round sequential. */
	readonly executionMode?: ToolExecutionMode;
	/**
	 * Repair arguments models commonly get wrong before validation, such as a JSON string where an array belongs. Must be
	 * pure and must not mutate `args`: it runs again when a call is retried before its intent is recorded. Its result is
	 * still validated against `parameters`.
	 */
	prepareArguments?(args: unknown): ToolArgs<TParameters>;
	/**
	 * Schema of `structuredOutput`, which programs that call the tool receive. Omitted: they receive the result's bounded
	 * output, success or error, as `NestedToolExecutionResult.structuredOutput` describes.
	 */
	readonly structuredOutputSchema?: object;
	/**
	 * Who may call the tool: the model, other tools through `executeTool()`, or both (default). A code mode tool is
	 * `["model"]`, so scripts cannot start scripts; tools behind code mode, such as MCP tools, can be `["tools"]`, so the
	 * model is never offered them.
	 */
	readonly callers?: readonly ("model" | "tools")[];
	/**
	 * Not offered to the model until loaded: the model gets the tool only when `modelTools` names it, in its array or its
	 * `add`, which `control.addTools` (from a tool such as `tool_search`) writes. Other tools can call it any time.
	 */
	readonly deferred?: true;
	readonly outputLimits?: {
		readonly maxBytes?: number;
		readonly maxLines?: number;
		readonly retain?: "head" | "tail";
	};
	/** A result, or a park (`ToolPark`): the call runs `execute()` again once woken. */
	execute(
		args: ToolArgs<TParameters>,
		api: ToolExecutionApi<TDetails, C>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<ToolExecutionResult<TDetails> | ToolPark<C>>;
	/**
	 * Clean up the external work of a call that parked, when it is aborted while no code of the tool runs (spec
	 * suspendable §4.2): `api.checkpoint` is the last park's, `api.wake` undefined, and it starts no nested calls or
	 * tasks. May run more than once, so idempotent. A throw is reported and the call still ends.
	 */
	cancel?(args: ToolArgs<TParameters>, api: ToolExecutionApi<TDetails, C>, context: Context): Promise<void>;
};

## UserInput  durable/src/harness/types.ts

## Wake  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/**
 * When a Session next needs a running process (`Harness.wake()`). `active`: some task can run now or is running, or a
 * reconcile pass such as open's recovery has not landed yet, so a process that dies must be woken again soon, for
 * example by a recovery alarm. `at`: the earliest sleep not yet due,
 * when there is one. Neither: nothing needs a process until new work is submitted. Tasks blocked on a missing or
 * unmigratable definition, `completing` tasks, and waits on live tasks do not count; the work they wait for does.
 */
export type Wake = { readonly active: boolean; readonly at?: number };

	| { readonly kind: "section"; readonly section: string; wrap(section: PromptSection<Tool>): PromptSection<Tool> };

## ConversationView  durable/src/harness/view.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Structural view of one conversation: a window over its transcript and its built-in documents (spec §9.3). */
export type ConversationView = {
	readonly conversation: ConversationRecord;
	/**
	 * A window over the transcript, its fork-aware history (`Conversation.entries()`), in entry ID order. Head markers
	 * such as compaction summaries sit where they were written; their `head` tells where the entries they summarize end.
	 */
	readonly entries: readonly EntryRecord[];
	/** ID of the entry just before the window; absent when the window starts the transcript. */
	readonly before?: EntryId;
	/** Built-in conversation documents keyed by kind; absent documents are absent. */

};

## ConversationWindow  durable/src/harness/view.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Which entries a view's window holds (spec §9.3). The window holds between `min` and `max` entries: it starts with
 * the newest `min` entries, takes appends, and once it would hold more than `max`, drops its oldest in one splice down
 * to `min`. With `from`, it starts at `from` instead when at most `max` entries are at or after it.
 */
export type ConversationWindow = {
	/**
	 * Where the first value's window starts, inclusive, such as right after the newest entry a client has
	 * (`ConversationTranscript.resume`). It selects only that first value: every entry committed after the attachment is
	 * appended, whatever its ID. A `from` past the newest entry starts the window empty, with `before` the newest entry.
	 */
	readonly from?: EntryId;
	/** Default 50; an integer, at least 1. */
	readonly min?: number;
	/** Default `2 * min`; an integer, at least `min`. */
	readonly max?: number;
};

	/** Positive integer version of the value shape. */
	readonly version: number;

};

## SignalResult  durable/src/signals.ts

/**
 * What a delivery did: `delivered` (durably accepted, not necessarily consumed), `duplicate` (the key holds a value),
 * `invalid` (not JSON, or not matching the schema), `closed` (the task ended, holds its outcome, is abort-marked, or the
 * key expired), `not_found` (no such task).
 */
export type SignalResult = "delivered" | "duplicate" | "invalid" | "closed" | "not_found";

## SignalState  durable/src/signals.ts

/** A key's state: the value delivered under it, or expired because its sleep's deadline came first. */
export type SignalState<T> = { readonly kind: "value"; readonly value: T } | { readonly kind: "expired" };

## SignalToken  durable/src/signals.ts

export interface SignalToken<T> {
	readonly name: string;
	readonly version: number;

}

## SubmissionSettled  durable/src/signals.ts
used by: durable-effect, swarm-effect
/**
 * Built in: delivered to `SubmissionDraft.notify` when the submission settles, in the settling commit. Its value is the
 * settled record, what `Submission.wait()` resolves to; its schema checks each variant's required fields, so another
 * delivery cannot take the key with something else.
 */
export const SubmissionSettled: SignalToken<(SubmissionRecordBase & { readonly type: "input"; } & { readonly status: "done"; readonly entry: EntryId; readonly answer: EntryId; readonly reason?: undefined; readonly detail?: undefined; } & { readonly status: "done" | "unanswered"; }) | (SubmissionRecordBase & { readonly type: "input"; } & { readonly status: "unanswered"; readonly entry?: EntryId | undefined; readonly answer?: undefined; readonly reason: string; readonly detail?: JsonValue | undefined; } & { readonly status: "done" | "unanswered"; }) | (SubmissionRecordBase & { readonly type: "write"; } & { readonly status: "done"; readonly entry: EntryId; readonly answer?: undefined; readonly reason?: undefined; readonly detail?: undefined; } & { readonly status: "done" | "unanswered"; }) | (SubmissionRecordBase & { readonly type: "write"; } & { readonly status: "unanswered"; readonly entry?: undefined; readonly answer?: undefined; readonly reason: string; readonly detail?: JsonValue | undefined; } & { readonly status: "done" | "unanswered"; }) | (SubmissionRecordBase & { readonly type: "continue"; } & { readonly status: "done"; readonly entry?: undefined; readonly answer: EntryId; readonly reason?: undefined; readonly detail?: undefined; } & { readonly status: "done" | "unanswered"; }) | (SubmissionRecordBase & { readonly type: "continue"; } & { readonly status: "unanswered"; readonly entry?: undefined; readonly answer?: undefined; readonly reason: string; readonly detail?: JsonValue | undefined; } & { readonly status: "done" | "unanswered"; })>

## readSignal  durable/src/signals.ts  watched
used by: durable-effect/src/signal.ts
why: P040: how Pi reads that memo; the facade reads it the same way.
/**
 * A key's state in `memos`, the value migrated to the token's version; undefined while nothing came. Throws for a stored
 * version newer than the token's, a missing or throwing `migrate`, or a migrated value the schema rejects.
 */
export function readSignal<T>(
	memos: Memos | undefined,
	token: SignalToken<T>,
	key: string,
): SignalState<T> | undefined {
	const stored = memoOf(memos, signalMemoName(token.name, key));
	if (stored === undefined) return undefined;
	if (stored.expired === true) return { kind: "expired" };
	if (stored.version === token.version) return { kind: "value", value: stored.value as T };
	if (stored.version > token.version) {
		throw new Error(`Signal ${token.name} value has version ${stored.version}, newer than ${token.version}`);
	}
	const { validator, migrate } = internalsOf(token);
	if (migrate === undefined) throw new Error(`Signal ${token.name} has no migration from version ${stored.version}`);
	const migrated = migrate(stored.value, stored.version);
	if (!isJsonValue(migrated) || !validator.check(migrated)) {
		throw new Error(`Signal ${token.name} migration from version ${stored.version} returned an invalid value`);
	}
	return { kind: "value", value: migrated as T };
}

## SignalMemo  durable/src/signals.ts  watched
used by: durable-effect/src/signal.ts
why: P040, P133: the shape of that memo ({ version, value } or { expired: true }).
/**
 * Stored state of one key, in the task's memo `pi.signal.<name>/<key>`, told apart by `expired`: the stored shape stays
 * as records already hold it.
 */
type SignalMemo = (ValueMemo & { readonly expired?: never }) | { readonly expired: true };

## signalMemoName  durable/src/signals.ts  watched
used by: durable-effect/src/signal.ts, approvals-effect/src/signal.ts
why: P040, P109, P133: a signal's state is read from the task's memo of this name.
/** The memo holding a key's state. Signal names contain no "/", so names never collide. */
function signalMemoName(signal: string, key: string): string {
	return `pi.signal.${signal}/${key}`;
}

## ValueMemo  durable/src/signals.ts  watched

## MemoryStorage  durable/src/storage/memory.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Detached in-memory reference implementation of `Storage`.
 *
 * Reads and retained writes are cloned intentionally to match the ownership boundary
 * of serialization-backed stores. This is backend conformance, not validation.
 */
export class MemoryStorage implements Storage {
	/**
	 * Apply `batches` one by one, each checked against the state the earlier ones left (`prepareCommit()`, which only
	 * checks and detaches, so a batch it refuses changed nothing); stops at the first one refused. Memory is durable at
	 * once; the receipts follow the last batch.
	 */
	async commit(
		batches: readonly (readonly StorageWrite[])[],
		receive: (index: number, seq: Seq) => void,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<CommitResult>
	/** Validate and detach one commit without changing observable state. */
	prepareCommit(writes: readonly StorageWrite[], seq: Seq = seqFromNumber(this.nextSeq)): PreparedMemoryCommit
	async mintId<I extends Id<string>>(): Promise<I>
	async conversation(id: ConversationId, _context: Context): Promise<ConversationRecord | undefined>
	async scanConversations(
		query: ConversationQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<ConversationRecord, Cursor>>
	entry(id: EntryId, context: Context): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>;
	entry(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		id: EntryId,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>;
	async entry(
		idOrConversationId: EntryId | ConversationId,
		idOrContext: EntryId | Context,
		context?: Context,
	): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>
	async findLatestHeadMarker(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		atOrBeforeEntryId: EntryId | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<(EntryRecord & { readonly head: EntryId }) | undefined>
	async scanEntries(
		query: EntryQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<EntryRecord, Cursor>>
	async task(id: TaskId, _context: Context): Promise<StoredTask | undefined>
	async scanTasks(
		query: TaskQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<StoredTask, Cursor>>
	async submission(id: SubmissionId, _context: Context): Promise<SubmissionRecord | undefined>
	async scanSubmissions(
		query: SubmissionQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<SubmissionRecord, Cursor>>
	async submissionByRequest(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		requestId: string,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<SubmissionRecord | undefined>
	async findDocument(
		address: DocumentAddress,
		at: DocumentPoint,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<DocumentRecord | undefined>
	async document(id: DocumentId, at: DocumentPoint, _context: Context): Promise<StoredDocument | undefined>
	async scanDocuments(
		query: DocumentQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<DocumentRecord, Cursor>>
	async close(_context: Context): Promise<void>
}

## PreparedMemoryCommit  durable/src/storage/memory.ts

/** A fully validated, detached state mutation whose application performs no fallible preparation. */
export interface PreparedMemoryCommit {
	readonly seq: Seq;
	/** Deeply frozen detached writes for persistence. */
	readonly writes: readonly StorageWrite[];

}

## SqliteStorage  durable/src/storage/sqlite/storage.ts
used by: durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/** Portable SQLite implementation of the Pico storage contract. */
export class SqliteStorage implements Storage {
	/** Initialize storage over an owned SQLite database facade. */
	static async open(db: SqliteDatabase, options: SqliteStorageOptions = {}): Promise<SqliteStorage>
	/**
	 * Commit `batches` in one SQL transaction, each with its own seq. Each batch is checked before it writes anything,
	 * against the state the earlier ones left, and the first one refused ends the batch: the transaction commits the ones
	 * before it. No savepoints, which Durable Objects do not allow: the checks run before the writes instead. The checks
	 * read the stored state of all batches up front and run in memory, and the accepted batches are written per table in
	 * multi-row statements (`commit.ts`), so a call costs a few statements whatever its number of batches. A batch with a
	 * copy reads the copy's source from the database: the batches before it are written first, so a call of many fork
	 * batches costs a few statements per fork.
	 */
	async commit(
		batches: readonly (readonly StorageWrite[])[],
		receive: (index: number, seq: Seq) => void,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<CommitResult>
	async mintId<I extends Id<string>>(): Promise<I>
	async conversation(id: ConversationId, _context: Context): Promise<ConversationRecord | undefined>
	async scanConversations(
		query: ConversationQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<ConversationRecord, Cursor>>
	entry(id: EntryId, context: Context): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>;
	entry(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		id: EntryId,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>;
	entry(
		idOrConversationId: EntryId | ConversationId,
		idOrContext: EntryId | Context,
		context?: Context,
	): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>
	findLatestHeadMarker(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		atOrBeforeEntryId: EntryId | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<(EntryRecord & { readonly head: EntryId }) | undefined>
	scanEntries(
		query: EntryQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<EntryRecord, Cursor>>
	async task(id: TaskId, _context: Context): Promise<StoredTask | undefined>
	async scanTasks(
		query: TaskQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<StoredTask, Cursor>>
	async submission(id: SubmissionId, _context: Context): Promise<SubmissionRecord | undefined>
	async scanSubmissions(
		query: SubmissionQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<SubmissionRecord, Cursor>>
	async submissionByRequest(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		requestId: string,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<SubmissionRecord | undefined>
	async findDocument(
		address: DocumentAddress,
		at: DocumentPoint,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<DocumentRecord | undefined>
	async document(id: DocumentId, at: DocumentPoint, _context: Context): Promise<StoredDocument | undefined>
	async scanDocuments(
		query: DocumentQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		_context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<DocumentRecord, Cursor>>
	close(_context: Context): Promise<void>
}

## CommitOptions  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings

## CommitPersistence  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via CommitOptions, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * When a commit reaches Storage. `immediate`, the default: before `commit()` resolves. `deferred`: when every write of
 * the commit changes an existing conversation document with `history: "latest"` and `fork: "initial"` (no creation,
 * migration, or retirement), the Session adopts it in memory, shows it to watches and views, and resolves, but stores it
 * later: with the next commit that reads (`tx.doc()`) or writes that document, before the document leaves memory or
 * retires, at `close()`, and at the latest about `withinMs` after the commit (default `settings.progress.persistWithinMs`,
 * 1,000 ms; `Infinity` waits for one of the others). A commit that writes anything else is immediate. A crash loses what
 * is held, so only state whose loss is acceptable, such as streamed progress, should be deferred, and nothing durable may
 * depend on it without reading it in a commit.
 */
export type CommitPersistence =
	| { readonly kind: "immediate" }
	| { readonly kind: "deferred"; readonly withinMs?: number };

## CommitPublication  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * Every immutable change one Session storage transaction stored, with its `seq`. Change order is unspecified. A commit
 * held in memory (`CommitPersistence`) is published once it is stored: by the next commit that reads or writes its
 * document, alone (`seq` of its own), or with that commit, whose document change then carries the held operations
 * followed by its own.
 */
export type CommitPublication = {
	readonly seq: Seq;
	readonly changes: readonly CommitChange[];
};

## CommitResult  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect via MemoryStorage, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage
/**
 * What `Storage.commit()` stored: the number of durable batches (`stored`: every one), and, when one was refused
 * (`refused`), why.
 */
export type CommitResult =
	| { readonly kind: "stored"; readonly stored: number }
	| { readonly kind: "refused"; readonly stored: number; readonly refused: unknown };

## CommonDocDefinition  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Definition fields shared by singleton documents and document families. */
export type CommonDocDefinition<T extends JsonObject> = {
	/** Stable persisted kind; part of the public protocol. */
	readonly kind: string;
	/** Positive integer version of the stored value shape. */
	readonly version: number;
	initial(): T;
	migrate?(value: JsonObject, fromVersion: number): T;
	/** Required policy: return true to store this ordinary change as a complete base instead of a delta. */
	checkpointWhen(value: Readonly<T>, ops: readonly Op[], info: CheckpointInfo): boolean;
};

## ContextEdit  durable/src/types.ts

## DocumentCommitChange  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via CommitPublication, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * Committed change of one document incarnation: `type: "document"` with `kind: "change"` (a creation or an update) or
 * `kind: "retire"` (this commit retired the incarnation), or a `document.copy`.
 */
export type DocumentCommitChange =
	| {
			readonly type: "document";
			readonly kind: "change";
			readonly record: DocumentRecord;
			/** Conversation owning the document; task documents derive it from their task record. Undefined only for Session documents. */
			readonly conversationId: ConversationId | undefined;
			/** Definition version of `value`. */
			readonly version: number;
			/** Exact adopted immutable revision. */
			readonly value: JsonObject;
			/** Exact adopted operations for an ordinary update; empty for creation. */
			readonly ops: readonly Op[];
	  }
	| {
			readonly type: "document";
			readonly kind: "retire";
			readonly record: DocumentRecord;
			/** Conversation owning the document; task documents derive it from their task record. Undefined only for Session documents. */
			readonly conversationId: ConversationId | undefined;
	  }
	| {
			/** Definition-free child initialization; consumers hydrate through watch acquisition. */
			readonly type: "document.copy";
			readonly record: DocumentRecord;
			readonly conversationId: ConversationId;
			readonly source: DocumentCopySource;
	  };

## DocumentRecord  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via MemoryStorage, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Persisted lifecycle record for one create-to-retire document incarnation. */
export type DocumentRecord = {
	/** Unique incarnation ID; never reused when the same logical document is recreated. */
	readonly id: DocumentId;
	/** Stable document definition kind. */
	readonly kind: string;
	/** Family member key; absent for singleton documents. */
	readonly key?: string;
	/** Commit that created the incarnation, stamped by storage. */
	readonly createdAt: Seq;
	/** Commit that retired the incarnation; absent while it is current. */
	readonly retiredAt?: Seq;
} & (
	| {
			readonly scope: { readonly kind: "session" };
			readonly history?: never;
			readonly fork?: never;
	  }
	| ({ readonly scope: { readonly kind: "conversation"; readonly conversationId: ConversationId } } & (
			| {
					/** Retain only current state. */
					readonly history: "latest";
					/** Initialize a fork from current source state or the definition's initial value. */
					readonly fork: "current" | "initial";
			  }
			| {
					/** Retain history needed for as-of reads. */
					readonly history: "rewindable";
					/** Initialize a fork at its cutoff, from current state, or from the initial value. */
					readonly fork: "asOf" | "current" | "initial";
			  }
	  ))
	| {
			readonly scope: { readonly kind: "task"; readonly taskId: TaskId };
			readonly history?: never;
			readonly fork?: never;
	  }
);

## DocumentSemantics  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Ownership and lifetime of a document; only conversation documents declare history and fork behavior. */
export type DocumentSemantics =
	| { readonly scope: "session"; readonly history?: never; readonly fork?: never }
	| LatestConversationSemantics
	| RewindableConversationSemantics
	| { readonly scope: "task"; readonly history?: never; readonly fork?: never };

## DocumentWatch  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via DocumentObserver, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * Watch of one document address (kind, scope, and key), from the incarnation found at acquisition on. A retirement is a
 * call with `retired` set, the last value the watch was given and no ops (a change made in the retiring commit itself
 * is not shown: that commit publishes the retirement only); the watch goes on, and a document created at the address
 * later arrives as `[["r", value]]`, folded with what is pending. It ends `ended` when its scope's owner ends: a task
 * document's watch once the retirement call of the commit that makes its task terminal returned, every watch at Session
 * close (a pending retirement dropped); `failed` with the error that failed the Session.
 */
export type DocumentWatch<T extends JsonObject> = WatchHandle<Readonly<T>>;

## EntryRecord  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect, durable-effect, guard-effect, recorder-effect, subagent-effect, swarm-effect, thread-effect; durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, review-effect via AssistantEntry
/** Immutable transcript event with separate model-facing and application-facing payloads. */
export type EntryRecord = {
	readonly id: EntryId;
	readonly conversationId: ConversationId;
	/** Application-defined entry discriminator. */

## HookRunner  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via TaskRuntime, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Dispatches one hook of a task to every matching registered handler, in registry order of the phase snapshot. */
export interface HookRunner<H extends object> {
	/**
	 * Call `invoke` with each matching handler named `name`. An ordinary throw from `invoke` is reported and the next
	 * handler runs; once the invocation is signalled, the error propagates. Composition happens inside `invoke`.
	 */
	each<K extends keyof H>(name: K, invoke: (handler: NonNullable<H[K]>) => void | Promise<void>): Promise<void>;
}

## JoinPolicy  durable/src/types.ts

/**
 * How a waiting task treats the tasks it waits on (spec §5.5): `allSettled` resumes once every task in `on` is terminal,

};

## NextTaskState  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * Next state a task commits for itself: a replacement checkpoint, a wait on tasks, a sleep, or its outcome. A returned `terminal` state is
 * stored as `completing` while ordinary owned work below the task is live (spec §5.5). A task never writes its own
 * `wake`: a commit of the same checkpoint keeps it, any other state drops it.
 */
export type NextTaskState<S, R> =
	| { readonly status: "running"; readonly checkpoint: S; readonly wake?: never; readonly outcome?: never }
	| Extract<TaskState<S, R>, { readonly status: "waiting" | "sleeping" | "terminal" }>;

## Observation  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** An attached `Observer`: the value at attachment, which every later `advance` starts from, and how to detach it. */
export type Observation<T> = {
	readonly value: T;
	/** Idempotent: no `advance` or `end` follows it, not even for the rest of a commit underway. */
	detach(): void;
};

## Observer  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/**
 * A synchronous observer of committed Durable state, for adapters such as a Chord source (`observeDoc()`,
 * `Harness.observeConversation()`, `Harness.observeTaskGraph()`), with the shapes of Chord's watch: `advance` gets a
 * `WatchCall`, `end` a `WatchEnd`. `advance` gets every change, unfolded, as memory adopts it: for a stored commit at its
 * publication once Storage stored it, for a deferred one before it is stored. A view or the graph gets at most one call
 * per commit, a document observer one per change at its address (two for a commit that retires and recreates it); the
 * task graph also advances outside any commit's publication, on the Session line, when a registry change or a failed
 * migration changes a
 * `blocked` reason. Durable's failures are final, so every call is a `value` call; a failure ends the observer. Calls
 * may come before the attaching promise resolves; their ops apply from `Observation.value`. `advance` must only record
 * the call, synchronously and quickly, never await, call the Session, or throw. A throw is reported as
 * `listener_error`, detaches the observer, and ends it `listener_error` with the error. `end` is called once: `ended`
 * when the observed scope's owner ends (a task document's task, after its retirement change, inside that commit's
 * `adopt`), `failed` with "session closed" when the Session closes (an adapter follows the next Session) or with the
 * error that failed the Session; never after `detach()`.
 */
export type Observer<T> = {
	advance(call: WatchCall<T>, context: Context): void;
	end(end: WatchEnd): void;
};

export type Page<T, C> = {
	readonly items: readonly T[];
	readonly next?: C;

## ReportInfo  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect via Report
/**
 * What a report to `HarnessOptions.onReport` is about, by `kind` (`Report` adds the error). `extension`, where present,
 * names the extension whose code failed, when known; for a task's own code, the one that installed the definition the
 * task ran.
 * - `storage_failed`: the error failed the Session, which closes: a Storage error, often a platform reset.
 * - `task_faulted`: the task ended `faulted`: its phase threw (`reason: "threw"`), or its abort handler was cut off
 *   `settings.restartLimit` times (`reason: "restart_limit"`), as was a phase of a task of an extension's kind.
 * - `task_interrupted`: crashes ended the task: it ended itself after being cut off `settings.restartLimit` times in a
 *   row (`reason: "restart_limit"`; a tool call, a compaction, a generation), or a generation's run ended because the
 *   host kept stopping while the model answered (`reason: "interrupted"`). `restarts` is the task's count when it ended.
 * - `migration_failed`: the task's stored state could not be migrated; it is blocked until the registry changes.
 * - `task_outdated`: a running task keeps running under its old definition, which was uninstalled (`missing_task`)
 *   or replaced by one that cannot take over its state: older than the task (`task_too_old`), or newer without a
 *   `migrate` (`migration_failed`).
 * - `task_error`: the task's own `runtime.report()`, or a failure in running it.
 * - `extension_error`: a hook, a section, a wrapper, or a tool's invalid structured output; with the task that ran it,
 *   or, outside a task, the conversation whose agent was resolved.
 * - `host_error`: a host callback threw; with the task that called it, if one did.
 * - `listener_error`: a commit, close, watch, view, or document listener threw.
 */
export type ReportInfo =
	| { readonly kind: "storage_failed" }
	| {
			readonly kind: "task_faulted";
			readonly task: ReportTask;
			readonly extension?: string;
			readonly reason: "threw" | "restart_limit";
	  }
	| {
			readonly kind: "task_interrupted";
			readonly task: ReportTask;
			readonly extension?: string;
			readonly reason: "restart_limit" | "interrupted";
			readonly restarts: number;
	  }
	| { readonly kind: "migration_failed"; readonly task: ReportTask; readonly extension?: string }
	| {
			readonly kind: "task_outdated";
			readonly task: ReportTask;
			readonly extension?: string;
			readonly reason: "missing_task" | "task_too_old" | "migration_failed";
	  }
	| { readonly kind: "task_error"; readonly task: ReportTask; readonly extension?: string }
	| {
			readonly kind: "extension_error";
			readonly extension?: string;
			readonly task?: ReportTask;
			readonly conversationId?: ConversationId;
	  }
	| { readonly kind: "host_error"; readonly callback: HostCallback; readonly task?: ReportTask }
	| { readonly kind: "listener_error" };

## Session  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via DocumentReader, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Owner of one mutation line, its records, and its tracked documents. */
export interface Session extends DocumentObserver {
	/**
	 * Run one atomic transaction on the Session mutation line. Inside the callback read only through `tx`: `snapshot()`, `watchDoc()`, `getTask()`, and the other Session and runtime reads may queue on the line the callback holds, and then never resolve.
	 * `options.persistence` may defer storing it (`CommitPersistence`). The callback may run while an earlier commit is
	 * being stored: at its first read or write of what an unpublished commit wrote, it waits until that commit is stored
	 * and published; code before that runs early, so act on what it computes only once the commit resolves. Resolves
	 * once the commit is stored and published, after every earlier commit's outcome.
	 */
	commit<T>(change: (tx: Tx) => T | Promise<T>, context: Context, options?: CommitOptions): Promise<T>;
	/** Seal admission, settle admitted commits, then close storage. */
	close(context: Context): Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * Settles once the Session has closed, Storage included: after `close()`, or after the first failed Storage call,
	 * which closes the Session itself. A failed Session is reopened from Storage; nothing else is left to clean up.
	 */
	readonly closed: Promise<SessionEnd>;
	/**
	 * Attach a synchronous `Observer` to one document address, atomically on the Session line, as `watchDoc()` acquires
	 * a watch: the observation's value includes every commit before it, and `advance` gets every later one, retirements
	 * and later incarnations included. `undefined` when the address is absent. `context` governs only the attachment:
	 * cancelled while attaching, the promise rejects and nothing stays attached.
	 */
	observeDoc<T extends JsonObject>(
		token: SessionDocToken<T>,
		observer: Observer<Readonly<T>>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Observation<Readonly<T>> | undefined>;
	observeDoc<T extends JsonObject>(
		token: ConversationDocToken<T>,
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		observer: Observer<Readonly<T>>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Observation<Readonly<T>> | undefined>;
	observeDoc<T extends JsonObject>(
		token: TaskDocToken<T>,
		taskId: TaskId,
		observer: Observer<Readonly<T>>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Observation<Readonly<T>> | undefined>;
	observeDoc<T extends JsonObject, I extends JsonValue>(
		token: SessionDocFamilyToken<T, I>,
		key: string,
		observer: Observer<Readonly<T>>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Observation<Readonly<T>> | undefined>;
	observeDoc<T extends JsonObject, I extends JsonValue>(
		token: ConversationDocFamilyToken<T, I>,
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		key: string,
		observer: Observer<Readonly<T>>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Observation<Readonly<T>> | undefined>;
	observeDoc<T extends JsonObject, I extends JsonValue>(
		token: TaskDocFamilyToken<T, I>,
		taskId: TaskId,
		key: string,
		observer: Observer<Readonly<T>>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Observation<Readonly<T>> | undefined>;
	/**
	 * Observe stored commits, each with exactly what it stored, except that a document the commit retires is published
	 * as its retirement only; a commit held in memory is published when it is stored (`CommitPublication`). Commits are
	 * published in line order once Storage stored them, a macrotask apart; a publication queues one dispatch, which runs
	 * a microtask later, before every wait the commit resolves and every abort it queues, and calls the observers
	 * attached by then; a commit published while none was attached has no dispatch. There is no order relative to watch listeners. `advance` runs synchronously and must not block or
	 * call Session APIs; a throw is reported as `listener_error`, detaches the observer, and ends it `listener_error`.
	 * `end` is called once, when the Session closes (`ended`, after its last publication) or fails (`failed`), never
	 * after `detach()`. Attaches synchronously; the observation has no `value`: commits are events, not a state, and the
	 * Session does not know Storage's newest `seq` before its own first commit.
	 */
	observeCommits(observer: CommitObserver): CommitObservation;
	/**
	 * Observe close synchronously when it begins, also when a failed Storage call closes the Session. The listener must
	 * not block or call Session APIs.
	 */
	subscribeClose(listener: () => void): () => void;

	snapshot<T extends JsonObject>(token: SessionDocToken<T>, context: Context): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;
	snapshot<T extends JsonObject>(
		token: ConversationDocToken<T>,
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;
	snapshot<T extends JsonObject>(
		token: TaskDocToken<T>,
		taskId: TaskId,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;
	snapshot<T extends JsonObject, I extends JsonValue>(
		token: SessionDocFamilyToken<T, I>,
		key: string,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;
	snapshot<T extends JsonObject, I extends JsonValue>(
		token: ConversationDocFamilyToken<T, I>,
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		key: string,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;
	snapshot<T extends JsonObject, I extends JsonValue>(
		token: TaskDocFamilyToken<T, I>,
		taskId: TaskId,
		key: string,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;

	snapshotAsOf<T extends JsonObject>(
		token: RewindableConversationDocToken<T>,
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		at: EntryId,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;
	snapshotAsOf<T extends JsonObject, I extends JsonValue>(
		token: RewindableConversationDocFamilyToken<T, I>,
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		key: string,
		at: EntryId,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Readonly<T> | undefined>;
}

## SetTimer  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect via HarnessOptions
/**
 * A host timer, given as `HarnessOptions.setTimer`: call `callback` once, about `delayMs` from now, and return
 * a function that disarms it. `background` timers only free memory, and a host may decline one by returning
 * `undefined`, for example where a pending timer keeps the process from hibernating; the Harness then frees that memory
 * at later commits. Other timers pace or resume work: one the host throws on or declines is armed with `setTimeout`.
 * A timer should not fire early; callers check their clock again when it fires.
 */
export type SetTimer = (
	callback: () => void,
	delayMs: number,
	options: { readonly background: boolean },
) => (() => void) | undefined;

## Storage  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage
/**
 * Atomic persistence boundary for Session records.
 *
 * Storage trusts the owning Session to supply semantically valid records, references,
 * ancestry, and transitions. Implementations enforce atomicity, global ID ownership,
 * immutable conversation/entry creation, document record consistency, and detached values;
 * Session serializes commits.
 *
 * An error a method throws is final: it fails the Session, which nothing retries, so retry transient failures inside
 * the method. Two errors of a read fail only that read: a `StorageRequestError` for an invalid request (an unknown
 * conversation, a foreign or malformed cursor, history a document does not keep), which must have no durable effect, and a
 * rejection because its caller's context was aborted. Any error from `commit()` or `mintId()` is fatal.
 */
export interface Storage {
	/**
	 * Persist `batches` in order, each as one ordinary atomic commit with its own seq, checked against the state the
	 * earlier ones left, in as few round trips as the backend can. Every batch has at least one write: a commit without
	 * writes never reaches Storage, so the Session never sends an empty batch. Stops at the first batch Durable's own checks refuse
	 * (global IDs, document actions, copy resolution): the batches before it are durable, it and the ones after are not.
	 * Calls `receive(index, seq)` once per durable batch, in order, synchronously, after all of them are durable and
	 * before the next commit starts. Resolves with the number of durable batches and the refusal, if any. Rejects for an
	 * unknown outcome (connection lost, statement or commit failed); `receive` calls made before the rejection still
	 * stand. `receive` is a durability receipt, not publication: the Session publishes later. Once it resolved, later
	 * reads through this storage observe the stored batches.
	 */
	commit(
		batches: readonly (readonly StorageWrite[])[],
		receive: (index: number, seq: Seq) => void,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<CommitResult>;

	/**
	 * Optional. Run `publish`, the Session's publication of one stored or held commit (its cache write-through,
	 * adoption, and observers), inside this storage's own scope, such as a store's attached host batch, so what the
	 * publication marks lands together. Call `publish` exactly once, now or soon after; the Session publishes the next
	 * commit only once it ran. Without it, the Session publishes directly.
	 */
	publishing?(publish: () => void, context: Context): void;

	/**
	 * Return a fresh branded candidate from the Session-global numeric ID namespace, greater than every ID minted since
	 * this storage was opened and every ID stored, also across reopen: scans order by ID as creation order, and the
	 * Harness relies on it.
	 */
	mintId<I extends Id<string>>(): Promise<I>;

	/** Look up one conversation by exact ID. */
	conversation(id: ConversationId, context: Context): Promise<ConversationRecord | undefined>;

	/** Scan conversations in `query.order` (default ascending) by ID. */
	scanConversations(
		query: ConversationQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<ConversationRecord, Cursor>>;

	/** Look up one global entry and the sequence of the commit that persisted it. */
	entry(id: EntryId, context: Context): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>;
	/** Look up one entry only when it is visible through the requested conversation's ancestry. */
	entry(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		id: EntryId,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<{ readonly entry: EntryRecord; readonly commitSeq: Seq } | undefined>;

	/**
	 * Return the newest visible entry with a `head` at or below the optional inclusive cutoff.
	 * The returned entry is the marker; its `head` value is the range's actual lower bound.
	 */
	findLatestHeadMarker(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		atOrBeforeEntryId: EntryId | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<(EntryRecord & { readonly head: EntryId }) | undefined>;

	/** Scan the inclusive visible range in `query.order` (default descending), returning at most `limit` entries. */
	scanEntries(
		query: EntryQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<EntryRecord, Cursor>>;

	/** Look up the latest complete record for one task. */
	task(id: TaskId, context: Context): Promise<TaskRecord<JsonValue, JsonValue, JsonValue> | undefined>;

	/** Scan task records matching every supplied filter in `query.order` (default ascending) by ID. */
	scanTasks(
		query: TaskQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<TaskRecord<JsonValue, JsonValue, JsonValue>, Cursor>>;

	/** Look up the latest complete record for one admitted submission. */
	submission(id: SubmissionId, context: Context): Promise<SubmissionRecord | undefined>;

	/** Scan submissions matching every supplied filter in `query.order` (default ascending) by ID. */
	scanSubmissions(
		query: SubmissionQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<SubmissionRecord, Cursor>>;

	/** Find a submission by its conversation-scoped host deduplication key. */
	submissionByRequest(
		conversationId: ConversationId,
		requestId: string,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<SubmissionRecord | undefined>;

	/** Resolve the incarnation occupying one exact logical address at the selected point. */
	findDocument(address: DocumentAddress, at: DocumentPoint, context: Context): Promise<DocumentRecord | undefined>;

	/** Materialize one specific incarnation by ID at the selected point without following a replacement at its address. */
	document(id: DocumentId, at: DocumentPoint, context: Context): Promise<StoredDocument | undefined>;

	/** Scan incarnations alive in one exact scope at the selected point. */
	scanDocuments(
		query: DocumentQuery,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<DocumentRecord, Cursor>>;

	/** Release backend resources; all later operations must reject. */
	close(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## StorageWrite  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via MemoryStorage, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** One record or document mutation in an atomic storage commit. */
export type StorageWrite =
	| { readonly type: "conversation"; readonly value: ConversationRecord }
	| { readonly type: "entry"; readonly value: EntryRecord }
	| { readonly type: "task"; readonly value: TaskRecord<JsonValue, JsonValue, JsonValue> }
	| { readonly type: "submission"; readonly value: SubmissionRecord }
	| {
			readonly type: "document.create";
			readonly record: DocumentCreate;
			readonly content: Extract<DocumentContent, { readonly kind: "base" }>;
	  }
	| { readonly type: "document.copy"; readonly record: DocumentCreate; readonly source: DocumentCopySource }
	| {
			readonly type: "document.change";
			readonly id: DocumentId;
			readonly content: DocumentContent;
	  }
	| { readonly type: "document.retire"; readonly id: DocumentId };

};

## SubmissionRecord  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect, thread-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via SettledSubmissionRecord
/** Durable lifecycle of one admitted user input, passive entry write, or continue. */
export type SubmissionRecord =
	| (SubmissionRecordBase & {
			readonly type: "input";
	  } & (
				| {
						/** Admitted but not yet represented in the transcript. */
						readonly status: "queued";
						readonly entry?: never;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason?: never;
						readonly detail?: never;
				  }
				| {
						/** Added to the transcript and owned by an active run. */
						readonly status: "placed";
						readonly entry: EntryId;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason?: never;
						readonly detail?: never;
				  }
				| {
						/** Successfully answered user input. */
						readonly status: "done";
						readonly entry: EntryId;
						readonly answer: EntryId;
						readonly reason?: never;
						readonly detail?: never;
				  }
				| {
						/** Terminal input that can no longer receive an answer. */
						readonly status: "unanswered";
						readonly entry?: EntryId;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason: string;
						readonly detail?: JsonValue;
				  }
			))
	| (SubmissionRecordBase & {
			readonly type: "write";
	  } & (
				| {
						/** Admitted but not yet appended to the transcript. */
						readonly status: "queued";
						readonly entry?: never;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason?: never;
						readonly detail?: never;
				  }
				| {
						/** Successfully appended passive entry. */
						readonly status: "done";
						readonly entry: EntryId;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason?: never;
						readonly detail?: never;
				  }
				| {
						/** Terminal passive write that could not be placed. */
						readonly status: "unanswered";
						readonly entry?: never;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason: string;
						readonly detail?: JsonValue;
				  }
			))
	| (SubmissionRecordBase & {
			/** A run started without a user message; it places no entry and is never queued. */
			readonly type: "continue";
	  } & (
				| {
						/** Owned by an active run. */
						readonly status: "placed";
						readonly entry?: never;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason?: never;
						readonly detail?: never;
				  }
				| {
						/** The run answered. */
						readonly status: "done";
						readonly entry?: never;
						readonly answer: EntryId;
						readonly reason?: never;
						readonly detail?: never;
				  }
				| {
						/** The run ended without an answer. */
						readonly status: "unanswered";
						readonly entry?: never;
						readonly answer?: never;
						readonly reason: string;
						readonly detail?: JsonValue;
				  }
			));

type SubmissionRecordBase = {

}

## TaskDefinition  durable/src/types.ts
used by: approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-effect via defineTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Executable durable state machine definition, registered in the registry by `name`. */
export type TaskDefinition<I, S extends { phase: string }, R, H extends object> = {
	/** Registered task kind persisted in `TaskRecord.kind`. */
	readonly name: string;
	/** Definition version persisted with live input and checkpoints. */
	readonly version: number;
	/** First durable checkpoint for a newly created task. */
	initial(input: I): S;
	/** Exhaustive phase map; each handler receives the task narrowed to its phase. */
	readonly phases: {
		readonly [P in S["phase"]]: PhaseHandler<I, Extract<S, { phase: P }>, S, R, H>;
	};
	/** Runs in a fresh invocation after an abort mark and must commit a terminal outcome. */
	abort(task: RunningTask<I, S, R>, runtime: TaskRuntime<I, S, R, H>, context: Context): Promise<void>;
	/** Convert a record stored by any older supported version; runs at reservation. */
	migrate?(
		input: JsonValue,
		checkpoint: JsonValue,
		fromVersion: number,
	): {
		input: I;
		checkpoint: S;
	};
	readonly hooks?: H;
};

## TaskOptions  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect, subagent-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via CompactionTask, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Creation options for a durable task. */
export type TaskOptions = {
	/** Omitted: inherit the creator's carrier. "root": start at the adapter root without a stored carrier. */
	readonly trace?: TelemetryCarrier | "root";
	/** Immutable creation-time links, attached to the spans of this task's first invocation. */
	readonly links?: readonly TelemetryCarrier[];
	/** Required: a task always names its owner (spec §5.5). */
	readonly ownership: TaskOwnership;
	/**
	 * Default: the owner task's conversation, or the transaction's bound conversation; required for conversation-owned
	 * tasks created by Session commits that are not bound to a conversation.
	 */
	readonly conversationId?: ConversationId;
	/** Conversation-owned tasks only: excluded from ordinary idle waits, conversation aborts, and cascades. */
	readonly background?: boolean;
	/**
	 * Its creator awaits it only in memory and does not resume after a restart, so it is pointless once the Harness that
	 * created it is gone. When scheduling starts in a later Harness, the task, if still live, is abort-marked with reason
	 * `restart`, and the mark cascades to its ordinary owned work, before any of it runs again.
	 */
	readonly abandonOnRestart?: boolean;
};

## TaskOutcome  durable/src/types.ts
used by: durable-effect; approvals-effect via ToolTask, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, guard-effect via ToolRegistration, subagent-effect via TaskState, thread-effect via HarnessSettings
/** Durable reason and optional result recorded when a task becomes terminal. */
export type TaskOutcome<R> =
	| {
			readonly status: "completed";
			readonly result: R;
			readonly error?: never;
			readonly reason?: never;
	  }
	/** Expected task or domain failure explicitly committed by its implementation. */
	| {
			readonly status: "failed";
			readonly error: TaskOutcomeError;
			readonly result?: R;
			readonly reason?: never;
	  }
	/** Explicit cancellation handled by the task's abort protocol. */
	| {
			readonly status: "aborted";
			readonly reason?: string;
			readonly result?: R;
			readonly error?: never;
	  }
	/** Task that cannot resume because its definition or migration is unavailable. */
	| {
			readonly status: "orphaned";
			readonly reason: string;
			readonly result?: never;
			readonly error?: never;
	  }
	/** Runtime-detected contract failure, such as an uncaught throw or no durable progress. */
	| {
			readonly status: "faulted";
			readonly error: TaskOutcomeError;
			readonly result?: never;
			readonly reason?: never;
	  };
